title: Inverse image preserves constructible modules with finite constant local models
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $\Lambda$ be an admissible coefficient ring: a finite commutative ring $A$ annihilated by a power of $\ell$ with its discrete topology, or one of $\mathbf Z_\ell,\mathcal O_E,\mathbf Q_\ell,E,\Qlb$ for a finite subextension $E\subseteq\Qlb$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, regarded as a condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], where $\Qlb$ means specifically the condensed ring of continuous maps with values in some finite subextension [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed]. Write $\Lambda(*)$ for its scalar ring. Let $g\colon Y'\to Y$ be a morphism of quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme, def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism], let $\Lambda_Y,\Lambda_{Y'}$ be the pulled-back coefficient sheaves on the small pro-étale sites [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], and let $g^*\colon\Mod_{\Lambda_Y}\to\Mod_{\Lambda_{Y'}}$ be the (underived) inverse image of module objects [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback].

Suppose $M$ is a constructible $\Lambda_Y$-module in the sense of [sk-def-sfb-constructible]: there is a finite stratification $Y=\coprod_{a}Y_a$ by constructible locally closed subschemes [def-constructible-stratification] such that each restriction $M|_{Y_a}$ has a finite constant local model [det-def-sfb-constructible-local-model], i.e. there are a pro-étale cover $\{U_{a,i}\to Y_a\}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] and finitely presented $\Lambda(*)$-modules $P_{a,i}$ with $M|_{U_{a,i}}\simeq\Lambda_{U_{a,i}}\otimes_{\Lambda(*)}P_{a,i}$. Then $g^*M$ is a constructible $\Lambda_{Y'}$-module in the same sense. More precisely, the subschemes $Y'_a=Y'\times_YY_a$ form a finite stratification of $Y'$ by constructible locally closed subschemes, and on $Y'_a$ the base-changed cover $\{U_{a,i}\times_{Y_a}Y'_a\to Y'_a\}$ and the same modules $P_{a,i}$ give a finite constant local model of $(g^*M)|_{Y'_a}$.

proof.text: Choose the finite stratification $Y=\coprod_aY_a$ given in the hypothesis. By [lemma-constructible-pullback-stratification], its base changes $Y'_a=Y'\times_YY_a$ form a finite stratification of $Y'$ with underlying strata $g^{-1}(|Y_a|)$. That statement supplies locally closed strata, not constructibility. Apply [lem-pur-scheme-constructible-preimage] separately to each constructible subset $|Y_a|\subseteq |Y|$: every $g^{-1}(|Y_a|)$ is constructible. Thus the proposed strata have both properties required here.

proof.text: For each stratum use the canonical Scheme.Cover.pullback₂ construction on the entire specified pro-etale cover [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. proof.text: Unpack finite presentation of each specified scalar module P [def-sfb-finitely-presented-module] as an isomorphism P ≅ coker(f) for f between finite free scalar modules. Define each scalar matrix entry as 1 followed by the corresponding component of f. The regular-module universal property and biproduct extensionality reconstruct f from these entries. Apply [lem-sfb-scalar-presentation-cokernel] to coker(f), its quotient map, and its cokernel universal property, on both old and new cover members. Composing with the scalar-extension image of P ≅ coker(f) gives the two model-to-matrix-cokernel isomorphisms with the same matrix and the same P.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-scalar-matrix-inverse-image] to $h$ and $A$ to obtain $h^*(M|_U)\cong\operatorname{coker}(A_V)\cong\Lambda_V\otimes_R P$. The two composites $V\to U\to Y$ and $V\to Y\prime\to Y$ are equal by the defining fibre-product square. The composition isomorphisms in [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback] therefore identify $h^*(M|_U)$ with $(g^*M)|_V$. This provides the required local isomorphism on every specified base-changed cover member.

That theorem pulls back the finite stratification [lemma-constructible-pullback-stratification] and applies [new-unbounded-pullback-finite-constant-local-model] on each stratum, using inverse-image composition to compare the restrictions. Its module and DAG dependency graph do not depend on this item. For the separately specified stratification, cover and scalar modules, apply steps 3-4 directly to the two nested fiber-product squares. The elementary predicate HasScalarModelOnRestriction names precisely the repeated isomorphism condition; it is an additional Lean attachment of this node, not a new mathematical lemma. The statement and generic comparison share this predicate, avoiding repeated expansion of inverse-image module objects during conversion. Use the actual pulled-back cover map and the actual immersion of constantModelPullbackStratification in the conclusion.
